claims.claim: Q2 2026 revenue rose 93% year over year to $1.935B, with U.S. commercial revenue up 149% and U.S. government revenue up 90%.
Palantir raised full-year revenue guidance to $8.150B-$8.158B and U.S. commercial guidance to more than $3.424B, reflecting accelerating operational-AI demand.

risks.risk: Revenue concentration is increasingly U.S.-weighted and government exposure can amplify policy/geopolitical sensitivity.

unknowns.unknown: Durability of exceptional growth rates beyond current AI adoption wave remains uncertain.

claims.claim: Q2 adjusted free cash flow reached $1.22B at a 63% margin and the company closed 220 deals worth at least $1M.

Recent reporting says Palantir is demanding stronger zero-data-retention guarantees from frontier-model providers, consistent with its stated sovereign-AI positioning but also evidencing third-party model/data-security dependency concerns.

risks.risk: Model-provider data-retention/security policy can constrain deployments involving sensitive proprietary data.

contradictions.contradiction: Explosive AI demand coexists with rising concern about third-party model data governance.

unknowns.unknown: Extent to which model-provider restrictions affect Palantir deployment economics or customer adoption is not quantified.
